In the figure below, the outside square contains infinitely many squares, each of them with the same center and sides parallel to the outside square. The ratio of the side length of each inner square to that of the next outer square is \(k,\) where \(0 \lt k \lt 1.\) The spaces between squares are alternately shaded, as shown in the figure (which is not necessarily drawn to scale).

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

The area of the shaded portion of the figure is \(64\%\) of the area of the original square. What is \(k?\)

In the figure below, \(ABEF\) is a rectangle, \(AD \perp DE,\) \(AF = 7,\) \(AB = 1,\) and \(AD = 5.\) What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

An array of numbers is constructed beginning with the numbers \(-1,\) \(3,\) \(1\) in the top row. Each adjacent pair of numbers is summed to produce a number in the next row. Each row will begin and end with the numbers \(-1\) and \(1,\) respectively. The first three rows are shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

If the process continues, one of the rows will sum to \(12{,}288.\) In that row, what is the third number from the left?

A circle of radius \(r\) is surrounded by three circles, whose radii are \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3,\) all externally tangent to the inner circle and externally tangent to each other, as shown in the diagram below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

What is \(r?\)

A Pascal-like triangle has \(10\) as the top row and \(10\) followed by \(1\) as the second row. In each subsequent row the first number is \(10,\) the last number is \(1,\) and, as in the standard Pascal’s Triangle, each other number in the row is the sum of the two numbers directly above it. The first four rows are shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

What is the sum of the digits of the sum of the numbers in the \(11\)th row?

The figure below shows an equilateral triangle, a rhombus with a \(60^\circ\) angle, and a regular hexagon, each of them containing some mutually tangent congruent disks. Let \(T,\) \(R,\) and \(H,\) respectively, denote the ratio in each case of the total area of the disks to the area of the enclosing polygon.

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Which of the following is true?

A circle has been divided into \(6\) sectors of different sizes. Then \(2\) of the sectors are painted red, \(2\) painted green, and \(2\) painted blue so that no two neighboring sectors are painted the same color. One such coloring is shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

How many different colorings are possible?

A container has a \(1 \times 1\) square bottom, a \(3 \times 3\) open square top, and four congruent trapezoidal sides, as shown. Starting when the container is empty, a hose that runs water at a constant rate takes \(35\) minutes to fill the container up to the midline of the trapezoids.

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

How many more minutes will it take to fill the remainder of the container?
